These passages concern the same original mortgage. The 1920 redemption was a subsequent event involving that mortgage, not a second original mortgage.

These connected findings and appellate framing support the full contextual premise without upgrading an attributed lower-court finding into an independently stated Supreme Court factual holding.

witnesses.quote: the other co-mortgagors should not be called upon to pay more than he paid in discharge of the encumbrance.
witnesses.reason: The Court explains the substantive limitation attached to equitable contribution.

witnesses.reason: Records Ganeshi Lal's alternative account of the character of his redemption, without independently proving it.

The two conclusions concern different aspects of one mortgage relationship.

witnesses.reason: The Supreme Court attributes this alternative assignment theory to counsel for Ganeshi Lal.

witnesses.quote: The registered deed of redemption does not contain any words of assignment.
witnesses.reason: The Supreme Court's evaluation of the instrument rejects the proposed contractual-assignment characterization.

The trial-court contribution finding identifies the plaintiffs and other interested co-sharers as the relevant counterparties. These sources collectively establish the full contextual premise. The remaining disputes about contribution amounts, final fractional shares and succession do not make the existence or subject of this controversy uncertain.
